model: RI-F500 series power analyser with RI-A5IPBAC BACnet IP module
applies_to: Rayleigh Instruments RI-F500 series panel power analysers fitted with the RI-A5IPBAC BACnet IP communication module and optional X1-X4 I/O extension modules.
summary: The RI-A5IPBAC is a BACnet IP add-on module for the RI-F500 series power analysers. Its object list is about 1,000 objects: 4-20 mA and PT100 inputs and 4-20 mA outputs on extension modules, Analog Values for voltages, currents, power, energy (per phase, per quadrant, tariffs and monthly history), max/min and demand values, harmonics up to the 63rd order, pulse counters and event records, writable setup values (CT/PT, demand, limits, relay and AO configuration), plus digital input, relay output and alarm status objects.
notes: Object names are the descriptions printed in the manual's object list; most are long, and the event-record objects repeat names like 'High byte: minute, Low byte: second'.
AV 7 is printed 'Phase current-I1' (same as AV 6); it is presumably I2.
Harmonic ratio objects are in 0.01 %; X1-X4 objects only work with the matching extension module fitted.
Writable configuration AVs pack options as integers (often high byte / low byte pairs); descriptions give the start of the printed option list.
BI objects for digital inputs are printed with access R/W.
BV status objects print the state meanings after the name (e.g. 'High voltage alarm, 0: no alarm occurs, 1: alarm occurs'); the name is the part before the first comma.
Source is a reseller's copy of the manual; no copy was found on rayleigh.com.

integration.summary: Configure the module's network settings from the RI-F500 front panel, then read total power, energy and the main voltages and currents. Set CT and PT values on the meter (or AV 788-793) before trusting the readings.
setup: The module's parameters are set through the RI-F500 meter, per the manual.
gotchas: Many objects only report data when the matching X1-X4 extension module is fitted.
Configuration AVs (784 onward) change meter setup; do not write them cyclically.
